Each opportunity is subject to disciplined due diligence, investment structuring and ongoing oversight, with a focus on long-term biological and real-asset exposure, potential risk-adjusted returns and measurable environmental and social outcomes. Partnership structures may be designed to combine Golden Forests’ agroforestry intelligence with established operators’ sector expertise, assets and market access. Golden Forests Holding is headquartered in Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM), UAE, with operating companies in the UAE and the Philippines and planned regional expansion across Asia.

Golden Forests combines local plantation execution with agronomic science, licensed cultivation technologies and AI-enabled monitoring to improve visibility across the asset lifecycle. Drone surveillance, predictive analytics and structured field data support earlier identification of operational risks, more informed cultivation decisions and transparent oversight. This integrated approach transforms plantation management from a largely manual activity into a disciplined, technology-enabled real-asset platform designed for long-term stewardship, resilience and measurable environmental and social value.

Contact our team about direct equity, independent regulated funds, direct plantation ownership, or joint ventures and strategic partnerships. Availability and eligibility depend on the selected opportunity and applicable requirements.

value: The current agarwood income model focuses on traceable, cultivated oud wood chips for specialist buyers. Resin content, aroma, quality, legal origin and documented chain of custody influence realized pricing. Oil, incense, fragrance ingredients and branded products are potential future opportunities, not the basis of the illustrative returns.
Golden Forests cultivates Aquilaria crassna in Negros Occidental, Philippines, combining nursery and field establishment, tree-health monitoring, inoculation readiness and resin development.
Agarwood provides the platform’s longer-duration crop exposure. Its commercial outcome depends on cultivation discipline, controlled processing, documented legal origin and successful sales.

Dwarf Sweet Elena mango combines Carabao mango seedlings grafted with Elena bud stock and managed through dwarfing techniques. The programme's premium Philippine fruit proposition is cultivated in Zambales Province, Philippines.

Nursery propagation, orchard establishment, pruning, crop protection and post-harvest quality support potential recurring harvests once trees mature. The illustrative model assumes annual harvests from Year 5 to 25; actual production and timing vary.

The commercial objective is premium Philippine mango supply for domestic premium channels, export-quality fruit programmes and branded produce relationships. Sorting, grading, packaging, cold-chain planning and buyer development are central to saleability and realized pricing.
Complementary Crops. Different Harvest Horizons.

The Philippine combined scenario pairs mango’s modeled recurring harvests from Year 5 with agarwood’s modeled harvest in Years 9–10. It illustrates a different cash-flow profile over 15 years; diversification does not eliminate agricultural, market or investment risk.
Two crops with different maturity and harvest profiles.

Charles McKenzie brings institutional fixed-income leadership from senior roles at Fidelity International, JP Morgan Asset Management, Aberdeen Asset Management and Deutsche Asset Management. At Fidelity he led more than 100 investment professionals across Europe and Asia. His experience supports board oversight, investment processes, risk controls and capital stewardship. He holds an MBA in Finance from Bayes Business School and a BSc (Hons) in Economics from the University of Southampton.

Mark Quinn is an international operating executive and entrepreneur with more than 35 years of experience in venture building, project finance, plantation operations, renewable energy and emerging-market execution. As founding President and CEO of CADI, he leads Philippine execution, operating partnerships and regional scale-up, bringing practical experience in nurseries, workforces, harvesting, processing, logistics, permitting and reporting systems.

Cord Kabus-Duprée brings international sales, client-management and business-development experience across investments, private equity, finance, family offices and strategic partnerships. He leads professional-investor outreach, commercial partnerships, strategic relationships and UAE market development, supported by financial-planning training and a master’s degree in business administration.

## Participation pathways
Golden Forests presents potential direct equity participation, participation through independent licensed and regulated fund partners, direct plantation ownership, and joint ventures or strategic partnerships. Each pathway requires opportunity-specific due diligence and final documentation. Fund offerings and materials are the responsibility of the relevant independent licensed entity. A company shareholding and direct plantation ownership are distinct arrangements.

## Illustrative return scenarios
The Philippine agarwood, mango and combined IRRs shown on this website are illustrative company scenarios reproduced from the November 2026 Investment Opportunities and Participation Overview. They use different time horizons and modeled cash flows, and are not forecasts, guaranteed returns, annual payouts, subscription terms or fund performance. They do not apply to Thailand opportunities. Actual investor outcomes depend on the selected structure, applicable documents and actual performance. Review the scenario assumptions and full financial models with independent advisers.

## Purpose of this website
This website provides general information about Golden Forests operating businesses and plantation activities. It does not provide investment, financial, legal or tax advice. Website content alone is not an offer or a commitment to issue shares or enter into a transaction.

## Direct company investment
Any direct equity transaction is an investment in the identified issuing company. A company share does not confer direct ownership of specific trees, planting blocks, land or other plantation assets. The identity of the issuer, share class, rights, price and transaction terms must be established in the relevant documents before any commitment.

## Eligibility and governing documents
Availability, eligibility, minimum investment and jurisdictional restrictions depend on the actual transaction and applicable law. Review the subscription and constitutional documents, share terms, risk disclosures, financial information and any relevant fee arrangements. Definitive transaction documents govern the transaction and prevail over summaries on this website. An enquiry does not constitute a subscription or acceptance.

## Investment risks
- Loss of some or all invested capital.
- No guarantee of returns, dividends, distributions, capital appreciation or repayment.
- Illiquidity, transfer restrictions, long investment horizons and potentially no secondary market.
- Agricultural, biological, weather, fire, pest, disease and natural-disaster risks.
- Operational, management, market, commodity-price, logistics and counterparty risks.
- Land-title, land-use, permitting, regulatory, political and legal risks.
- Currency, taxation and cross-border investment risks.
- Valuation uncertainty and delays in development, harvesting, sales or exits.
- Concentration and private-company risks, including insolvency.

## Business revenues and shareholder outcomes
Harvest proceeds belong to the relevant business and are not automatically payable to shareholders. Any dividends depend on company performance, available cash, reserves, share rights and applicable law. Plantation records and inspections do not guarantee asset value, title, liquidity or investor returns.

## Forward-looking and environmental statements
Plans, forecasts and illustrative operating timelines depend on assumptions and actual conditions. They are not guarantees of future results. Environmental objectives, including biodiversity and carbon-related outcomes, require implementation, measurement and verification. No certified carbon credits or certification status should be inferred from an objective or estimate.

## Reporting and third parties
Company financial reports, plantation inspections and independent audits serve different purposes. Their availability and scope must be confirmed in the relevant company arrangements. References to research, technical or operational partners do not imply their endorsement of an investment or a guarantee of its results.

## Independent advice
Prospective investors should assess their circumstances, liquidity needs, risk tolerance and investment horizon and obtain independent advice from appropriately qualified financial, legal, tax and accounting professionals. Do not act on this website where doing so would breach applicable law. Accessing this website does not create an advisory relationship, an investment commitment or a waiver of legal rights.
